stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

Below is a quick‑start guide for one of the most popular public services that turns an IPv4 / IPv6 address into “company”‑level metadata—including optional contact fields—when it’s available: | Service | Key Features | Free Tier Limits | Typical Contact Fields Returned | |---------|--------------|------------------|--------------------------------| | **ipapi** (`https://ipapi.co`) | • Organization & ASN
• Company name + domain
• Email & phone when supplied by ISP | 30 k lookups/month; 60 req/minute | `org`, `asn_org_name`, `email` (rare), `phone_number` (rare) | | **IPStack** (`http://api.ipstack.com`) | • Business name & industry
• Domain owner email & phone | 10 000 monthly queries; 200 req/hour | `business_name`, `industry`, `domain_owner_email`, `domain_owner_phone` | | **IpGeolocatioN.io** (`https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo`) | • Company name & website
• Support contacts | 15 000 daily queries; 500 req/day for paid plans | `organization_name`, `website_url`, `support_contact_email`, `support_contact_phone` | --- ### Why this works These APIs usually pull their data from: * WHOIS registries – giving you the registered corporate entity behind the IP block. * Public DNS records – sometimes exposing mail exchange hosts linked to a company. * Proprietary databases built from partner ISPs and BGP feeds – adding extra context like support emails or phone numbers. When the provider has no explicit contact record attached to the IP range, the service simply omits those keys rather than fabricating them. --- ## Quick Example Using *ipapi* ```bash curl -s https://ipapi.co//json/ ``` Python wrapper (no external library needed): ```python import json, urllib.request def get_company_info(ip): url = f"https://ipapi.co/{ip}/json/" try: resp = urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=5) return json.loads(resp.read().decode()) except Exception as e: print(f"Error fetching data: {e}") return None data = get_company_info("8.8.8.8") print(json.dumps(data, indent=2)) ``` Typical JSON output (fields omitted if unavailable): ```json { "ip": "8.8.8.8", "city": "Mountain View", "region": "California", "country_code_iso2": "US", "postal": "94035", "latitude": 37.386, "longitude": -122.0838, "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles", "currency": "USD", /* Company-level */ "org": "Google LLC", "asn": "AS15169", "as_description": "GOOGLE", /* Optional contact – rarely present */ "email": "dns-admin@google.com", # <-- only if the registry publishes it "phone_number": "+1-650-253-0000" # <-- same caveat } ``` If you’re building a production system, consider caching the result locally because repeated lookups hit rate limits quickly. --- ## Things To Keep In Mind | Issue | Mitigation | |-------|------------| | **Privacy** | Some jurisdictions restrict publishing personal/company contact info. Always respect local laws. | | **Accuracy** | Data comes from third parties; double‑check critical fields before acting on them. | | **Rate Limiting** | Use exponential backoff or queue requests if you exceed quotas. | | **Data Freshness** | Registrations change often; cache aggressively but refresh at least once per day for high‑value assets. | Feel free to let me know what kind of integration you have in mind (webhook, batch job, real‑time lookup?) so I can suggest more tailored code snippets!
